claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children for whom you're looking to claim Child Benefit? If yes, could you please tell me:
- How many children you have?
- Their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now, are you responsible for Alex? This usually means either:
- You live with Alex, or
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after Alex - for example on food, clothes or pocket money

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards their upkeep - things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To understand your situation better, I need to ask:

Who does Alex currently live with, and how long has Alex been living with them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with their other parent, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Now I need to understand the financial contributions you're making:

How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep (for things like clothes, school supplies, etc.), and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One more important question:

Is your ex-partner (the person Alex lives with) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with your ex-partner
- You contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- Your ex-partner is not currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the rules, you can continue to get Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else if you contribute to their upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, and you're contributing £50 per week, which is well above this threshold.

Since you're making regular financial contributions that exceed the Child Benefit amount, and no one else is claiming for Alex, you should be eligible for Child Benefit.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.
